raw.transcript:
If you don’t know the router password, don’t worry, you still have options. First, check the sticker on the router itself. Many routers list a default admin username and password there.

Next, try common defaults like “admin” and “admin,” or “admin” and “password.” If those don’t work, you can reset the router by holding the reset button, usually for about 10 seconds, but that will erase custom settings.

After a reset, you’ll log in with the default password and set a new one. If you’re renting the router from your internet provider, you can also call them, and they can help you regain access without guesswork.
